objective: Take up WEAK-APER-20261110-001's direction 1 (the same as RIGID-WORLDS-20261110-001#3 and BOARD-DIST-20261110-001#3) at the coordinator's go-ahead of 2026-11-10: challenge A54 by naming places without letters. Names are a countable set with no structure; each pair of names has a neighbour distinction and each name a value; laws are uniform over names. Ticket A proves what a law can then force: finitary laws always allow a structureless board (Ramsey); existence clauses supply a degree, and every board with even degree 2k carries k permutations, so the letters draw degree and connectivity and nothing more; count laws allow the universal cover of every board (the unfolding theorem without letters); no first-order law forces connected boards, and a named face with aperiodic tiles makes every component a plane; and boards are not frozen without letters, since edges with the same pair of values can exchange partners. Ticket B runs a frozen census of the 1,024 one-bit count laws: which knot the board with the values, and whether those knots are native.
status: Complete 2026-11-10 (Successful): the challenge of A54 answered by proof and a frozen exact census. With places named without letters (a countably infinite set of names, a neighbour distinction per pair), every finitary law that allows a state allows a structureless one (Ramsey), so none forces a neighbour; a degree from existence clauses carries a labelling no clause can read; count laws allow every cover of their boards, hence a tree whenever a cycle; no law of bounded degree forces a connected board, and a named square with aperiodic tiles gives tiled planes componentwise; boards are not frozen (two edges with one pair of values exchange partners), and 90 of the 1,024 one-bit count laws knot one neighbour distinction with its two endpoint values; renamings make the source-aware condition exclude nothing (A59). By the frozen rule A54 is confirmed for the obstruction, and the frozen boards of BOARD-DIST-20261110-001 rest on the naming. Read by an independent referee before publication. Recommendation Research directions, selected #1 (nativeness up to renaming).
